newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end higher as U.S. data drives Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end higher as U.S. data drives Dow rally.

text.p: ** UK shares end mostly higher as weaker-than-expected wage
inflation data spurs Dow rally. Dow up 93 at UK close.
** Data seen making February U.S. rate rise less likely.
** LucasVarity jumps after trading statement.
** RMC squeezed higher after Cazenove comment.

"A lot of people were worried that we'd see a high number, which would really bash the Street," one dealer said. "There was a lot of relief when it came out and some of the fears about a correction on Wall Street have been reduced."
Analysts said the UK interest-rate outlook had become more bullish in recent days and if Wall Street held its nerve the FTSE could revisit its record high of 4,273.4 this week.

"If Wall Street is relatively well-behaved, then the UK market probably still has a good deal of support in the near-term," said Richard Kersley, UK equities strategist at BZW. "The risk is now more external than domestic."
Dealers said the FTSE continued to be supported by strong buying interest which was sqeezing prices higher.

"There still is a lot of liquidity in the hands of institutions and it is difficult to see in the short term where there will be any sustained selling," said the head of UK equity sales at a major investment bank.

"In some ways the market is overvalued but in a liquidity-driven market prices will always go higher than is jsutified by the fundamantals," he said. "If the Dow doesn't crack, and continues to hold up, it's difficult to see the FTSE running out of steam just yet."
Trading volumes in London were up on Monday's levels as investors returned to the market once the U.S. data was out of the way. Volume on SEAQ was 822 million by 1701 GMT.

LucasVarity was the FTSE's best performing stock, ending 13-1/2p or 6.5 percent higher after a trading statement that was optimistic on growth in 1997 and soothed investors' fears of a further dividend cut.
Building materials group RMC climbed 38-1/2p to 975, squeezed higher after a Cazenove recommendation created a shortage of stock, dealers said. Redland was also strong, up 17p at 354-1/2.
Food retailers, hit by selling in recent sessions, reclaimed some lost ground. Marks & Spencer rose 16-1/2p to 493-1/2 ahead of a trading statement due on Wednesday.
ASDA gained 3-1/4p to 123-1/2, Tesco rose four pence to 359 and Safeway SFY.L climbed six pence to 382.
Imperial Tobacco ended 12p higher at 396-1/2, after it announced the 185 million stg acquisition of Rizla, the world's biggest maker of handrolling tobacco papers.
On the downside, Tate & Lyle fell to a six-month low on talk that analysts at NatWest had futher cut their profit forecasts. It ended 12p weaker at 429-1/2.

The property sector also retreated. Great Portland Estates fell eight pence to 207-1/2 after a rights issue and MEPC eased 6-1/2p to 448-1/2, after negative comments from analysts at ABN Amro Hoare Govett. Land Securities was down 10p at 757-1/2.
-- Andrew Marshall, London newsroom +44 171 542 4367
